summary: Re-tested billing expiry refactor after fix. The critical _create_first_invoice bug is RESOLVED. 10/11 backend tests PASS; 1 test (cron generate in-notice-window) FAILS due to a separate pre-existing data issue: the seeded operator document has NO `status` field in Mongo, so the cron query `{status: {$in: ['active','trial']}}` matches 0 operators (total_checked=0) and no upcoming invoices are ever generated for it. Frontend regression passed: login, Add Subscriber dialog with plan_start_date & 'Generate First Invoice Now?' toggle, and Invoices list all render and the previously-failing generate_first_invoice flow now yields invoices visible in the list.

minor.issue: Returns total_checked=0 because the seeded operator (cc00cc66-b87c-4e1d-997f-d1bf9dd09743 / operator@test.com) has no `status` field in MongoDB (value is None / missing). The cron query uses {status: {$in: ['active','trial']}} which excludes documents without that field. Admin /api/admin/operators normalises missing status to 'active' so the UI/tests can't see the gap. Impact: cron will SILENTLY skip any legacy operator whose status field was never written — including this main test operator. Fix options: (a) migration to backfill `status='active'` on operators where missing, (b) change cron query to `{status: {$ne: 'suspended'}}` (treat missing as active), or (c) always set status on operator creation.

issues: Plan Start Date still uses native <input type='date'> instead of shadcn Calendar (minor inconsistency — flagged in iteration 18, not yet addressed).

action_items: Backfill operator.status='active' for the seeded operator (and any other legacy operators) so cron generate_upcoming_invoices can process them. One-liner: db.operators.update_many({status: {$exists: false}}, {$set: {status: 'active'}}). Alternatively make the cron tolerant of missing status.
Optional: switch Add Subscriber Plan Start Date to shadcn Calendar component.

Consider removing the broad `except Exception` around _create_first_invoice invocation in routers/operator.py (line ~1283) — it was promoted to ERROR + exc_info in this iteration, which is good, but the failure is still swallowed so the API returns 200 with no invoice. Surface a warning in the response payload (e.g. `{subscriber, invoice_generation_failed: true, reason}`).
critical_code_review_comments: services/cron_service.py:693-694 fix is correct — `from utils import generate_invoice_number_atomic; invoice_num = await generate_invoice_number_atomic(self.db)` is the same pattern used elsewhere in the file. Verified end-to-end.

services/cron_service.py:74-78 `operators.find({'status': {'$in': ['active','trial']}, ...})` is fragile — any legacy operator without a status field is silently excluded. Either ensure all operator inserts write `status` or relax the query.

routers/operator.py:1947 try/except for expiry-extension still logs at WARNING and silently continues. Extension verified working now, but the silent swallow is still a risk for future regressions — log at ERROR with exc_info like the first-invoice try/except was updated to.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The _create_first_invoice bug and mark-paid expiry extension are both fully verified working. The only remaining blocker on cron upcoming-invoice generation is operator.status being missing in Mongo. If main agent runs the status backfill, test_cron_creates_invoice_when_in_notice_window should turn green — re-run just that single test after the fix: `pytest tests/test_billing_expiry_refactor.py::TestCronGenerateUpcomingInvoices::test_cron_creates_invoice_when_in_notice_window -v`.
rca of the issue: The cron generate_upcoming_invoices function filters operators with {status: {$in:['active','trial']}}. The test operator (operator@test.com, id=cc00cc66-b87c-4e1d-997f-d1bf9dd09743) was seeded without a `status` key in its MongoDB document. Admin list endpoints add a default 'active' on the fly so the field appears present in APIs, but the raw cron query returns 0 matches. REPRODUCTION: `db.operators.find({status:{$in:['active','trial']}}).count()` returns 0 while `db.operators.count()` returns 1. MITIGATION: backfill with `db.operators.update_many({status:{$exists:false}}, {$set:{status:'active'}})` OR update the cron to treat missing status as active.
